title: Shelf Descriptor (capability-level, v1)
description: The durability artifact for ONE reusable CAPABILITY (a multi-component process), not a single component. Defined by Projects-tab-v3 North Star (docs/projects-tab-v3-north-star.md) §8 — the reuse/shelf durability mandate. A capability is a whole process (e.g. funnel -> pipeline -> brainstorm -> spec -> build -> closeout) authored once and adopted by future surfaces/products as assembly rather than rebuild. The §8 fields are named verbatim: capability statement, contracts, reuse_mode, seams, invariants. This schema adds (a) reuse_boundary — the generic-vs-surface-specific line the North Star §8 + spec §3 draw — and (b) component references, so the capability descriptor points at the per-COMPONENT cards on the ourliberty-graph shelf (descriptors/*.json, the v2 Component Descriptor schema) rather than restating them. GRANULARITY NOTE: ourliberty-graph/descriptors/descriptor.schema.json catalogs ONE component (a file/module); THIS schema catalogs ONE capability (a cluster of components forming a reusable process). They are complementary, not competing. RUNTIME COUPLING: this is a documentation artifact. Nothing in the running system reads a shelf descriptor at runtime in this cut (North Star §8; spec §5.4 guardrail — 'Descriptor is documentation, not a coupling'). It is kept honest by mirroring the real seams of the components it catalogs, not by being load-bearing config.

schema_version.description: Bumped only on a breaking shape change. Readers tolerate-and-ignore unknown additive keys.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id for the capability (the librarian's lookup key). e.g. 'projects-v3-universal-card'.

north_star_ref.description: Path + section anchor of the doc that mandates this capability's reuse (e.g. 'docs/projects-tab-v3-north-star.md §8').

source_repos.description: The repo(s) the capability's components live in (the capability commonly spans more than one — e.g. agent-core authoring + dashboard rendering).

consumers.description: Who renders/adopts this capability today, and which surfaces/products are intended adopters. The first consumer is the surface it was authored on; later entries are the durability payoff (other tabs, other products).

capability_statement.description: §8 field. Plain-language 'what the whole capability does' — the one paragraph a stranger reads to decide whether to adopt it instead of rebuilding. Describes the PROCESS end to end, not any one component.

contracts.description: §8 field. The interface contracts the capability exposes to (or consumes from) the rest of the system — the stable shapes a new surface binds to. NOT a per-function signature dump (that lives on the component cards); these are the capability-level contracts: the data shapes, the action set, the event triggers, and the authoring/render split that a new adopter must honor.

kind.description: What sort of contract this is.

description.description: The contract in plain language: what it guarantees and what an adopter must satisfy.

generic_or_surface_specific.description: Whether this contract is the same for every surface (generic) or supplied per surface (surface-specific). Cross-references reuse_boundary.

reuse_mode.description: §8 field. How this capability is reused. A capability is rarely a single liftable unit; it is usually assembled from already-generic components plus a small surface-specific layer.

mode.description: assembly-of-shelf-components = reuse the existing generic components and write only the surface-specific seam (the common case for a mature capability); liftable-cluster = lift the whole component set together; pattern-to-reimplement = the shape is the reusable thing, reimplement per host.

rationale.description: Why this mode — what is already generic vs what each new surface must author.

reuse_boundary.description: The generic-vs-surface-specific boundary the North Star §8 + spec §3 draw — the single most important field for an adopter, because it says exactly what they get for free and what they must supply. This is what makes a new surface 'assembly, not a rebuild'.

generic.description: What is the SAME across every surface — the parts an adopter reuses verbatim.

surface_specific.description: What each surface must SUPPLY — the parts that carry the difference (typically: which registry the items live in, the available action set, and the context the authoring layer reads).

seams.description: §8 field. The integration points where the capability meets the rest of the system AND where a new surface plugs in. Must MIRROR the real seams of the catalogued components (the spec §5.4 honesty mandate) — a seam here should be traceable to a seam on a component card, not invented.

invariants.description: §8 field. The discipline that must hold for the capability to stay correct as it is reused — the rules an adopter must not break (single-committer, doorbell, plain-language-always, event-not-poll, no-raw-metadata-leak, etc.). Mirror the real component invariants.

components.description: The per-component shelf cards (ourliberty-graph descriptors/*.json) this capability composes. Pointers, not copies — the component cards own the per-file contract; this list says which ones assemble into the capability and what role each plays.

component_id.description: The id of the component's shelf card (e.g. 'projects_store') — resolves to ourliberty-graph/descriptors/<id>.json.

role.description: What this component does within the capability.

layer.description: Which side of the reuse boundary this component sits on.

runtime_coupling.description: Encodes the spec §5.4 guardrail structurally: the descriptor is documentation, not a coupling. Nothing reads it at runtime in this cut.

status.description: MUST be 'none' — a shelf descriptor that becomes load-bearing config has drifted from its purpose.

note.description: How the descriptor is kept honest despite nothing reading it (by mirroring the real component seams; reviewed at authoring time).

sources.description: Where the seams/invariants were mirrored from (the component cards + specs read to author this descriptor).
